newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: INSTANT VIEW-Bank/Portugal leaves drain rate.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Bank/Portugal leaves drain rate.

text.p: Here are some analysts' reactions to the Bank of Portugal's decision not to cut its drain rate, the rate at which it absorbs excess funds, for the start of a new commercial bank reserve period. The rate is 6.2 percent.
RUI MARTINS DOS SANTOS, BANCO PORTUGUES INVESTIMENTO

"It is a cautious stance at a time when the (year-on-year) inflation rate is likely to rise in January and February. Another interpretation could be that it does not want to follow Spain. There is still clear room for a rate cut because the escudo is firm against the mark even if it reflects moves in other periphery currencies rather than capital flows."
JORGE FERRAZ, IMF-INFORMACAO DE MERCADOS FINANCEIROS

"I think that the Bank is concerned about inflation in January and February. I think that (as it did not cut) money market rates could rise a little. If the Bank of Portugal does not cut the repo rate immediately after the (next) Bundesbank meeting, it is going to wait for the January inflation numbers.

"I was expecting a cut. I am convinced that inflation is under control but there is still a sector -- non-tradable goods -- that needs to come down and perhaps it is possible by means of interest rates. Besides that, there remains the old question of drawing a line between us and Spain. But (the leaving of the rate unchanged) does not put in question, in any way, the belief that inflation is under control and that (interest) rates are going to go down.
